title: Screen Time in the Early Years: Content Quality and Suitable Boundaries
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics’ (AAP) statement published on 20 January 2026 focuses on content quality and family needs, while prioritising sleep, play, movement and reading. It says time limits might be less than one hour daily for toddlers and preschoolers, and clinicians can discuss boundaries that fit a family’s routine. The statement explains that infants do not learn from digital media, but occasionally viewing a brief, high-quality video is not detrimental; this does not recommend regular viewing or replacing direct interaction with screens. WHO’s 2019 guidelines do not recommend screen time for infants or sedentary screen time for one-year-olds, and limit it to one hour daily at age two; less is better. Each organisation’s position is presented separately. Make time for sensory play, movement, reading and direct interaction with your child.
try_this: This week: Try a 'zero screens hour' daily—put the phone in another room, get down on the floor with your child, and play together with anything available (plastic containers, pots, cloth balls). Notice: Does he interact more? Does he sleep better? Record your observations.
reflection_prompts: What is the hardest moment in your day when you tend to hand your child a screen? What is a possible alternative?
Have you noticed a difference in your child’s behavior after a screen-free day?
